newsitem.title: UK: ICI sees H2 profit improving after Q1 fall.
newsitem.headline: ICI sees H2 profit improving after Q1 fall.

text.p: British giant Imperial Chemical Industries Plc on Thursday reported sharply lower first-quarter profits, but added that it saw results improving in the second half of 1997.
First quarter pre-tax profit before exceptional items fell to 65 million pounds ($105.6 million) from 202 million in the year-ago period.
Analysts had forecast the firm's pre-tax profits at 75-90 million pounds, with the consensus estimate around 79 million.
ICI said the current strength of the pound reduced profits by 40 million pounds, while the currency adversely affected sales by six percent.

"It is widely forecast that the growth in OECD chemical production will be higher in 1997 than last year, so it is expected that profits in the second half will show improvement," ICI chairman Sir Ronald Hampel said in a statement.
ICI's shares were marked down 15.5 pence at 705 by 0710 GMT.

The firm said demand was robust in most territories and businesses, especially in its Industrial Chemicals and Materials unit, but sales prices were hurt by the cyclical downturn in the Polyester and Tioxide sectors.
Trading profits at its paints business more than doubled to 30 million pounds in the quarter -- the unit's seasonally weakest period -- boosted by acquisitions, cost controls, and lower input prices.
